pick.name: Zoho Books Free
pick.what: GST invoices, quotes, payments, inside your accounting ledger
pick.why: One free tool for invoicing + books + GST returns; CA-friendly; avoids double entry
pick.free_limits: Free while FY revenue <= Rs25 lakh; 1,000 invoices/yr; 1 user + 1 accountant; GST returns included; NO multi-currency (Professional+) and no e-invoicing on Free

alts.name: Invoice Ninja
alts.what: Invoicing with multi-currency, client portal, recurring
alts.why: Use for USD/EUR export invoices while Books Free lacks multi-currency
alts.free_limits: Hosted free: up to 5 clients (some reviews say 20), unlimited invoices; Pro $14/mo; self-host under Elastic License 2.0 (own use OK, no hosted resale)

alts.name: Zoho Invoice (India)
alts.free_limits: 2 users, 3 projects, 500 invoices/yr; KB: 'you can invoice your customers only using your base currency'; data deleted after 180 days inactivity

candidates.name: Skydo invoicing
candidates.verdict: Bundled if you use Skydo (not verified)

decision: Most global card revenue is invoiced by the MoR, so you only invoice B2B services and Indian clients; Zoho Books Free covers that plus GST returns. Issue USD export invoices from Invoice Ninja (or upgrade Books to Professional) until volume justifies it.
details: Export invoices under LUT must carry the LUT reference and 'supply meant for export under LUT without payment of IGST' wording (verify with CA).

verify.note: Zoho Books pricing: Free under Rs25L FY revenue, 1,000 invoices + 1,000 bills/expenses/yr, 1 user + 1 accountant, GST filing; multi-currency only from Professional; e-invoicing from Standard. Zoho Invoice KB confirmed: 'you can invoice your customers only using your base currency in Zoho Invoice' (Zoho points to Zoho Billing for multi-currency).
